$ ergon tool --help
Usage: ergon tool <command> [options]

Run the tools that the sections of .ergon.yaml name.

ergon tool runs the tools that the sections of .ergon.yaml name, at the
versions that they name. Every target of the Makefile and every hook of the
baseline of ergon init runs its tools this way.

Commands:
  run    Install a tool of a section and run it.
  path   Install a tool of a section and print its program.
  prune  Remove the tools that no section of .ergon.yaml names.
  ci     Run the jobs that keep the tools of ergon in GitHub Actions.

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon tool ci --help
Usage: ergon tool ci <command> [options]

Run the jobs that keep the tools of ergon in GitHub Actions.

ergon tool ci runs the steps of the jobs of the managed workflows that keep the
tool directory of ergon in the cache of GitHub Actions.

Commands:
  prune  Delete the tool caches that newer caches replaced.

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon tool run --help
Usage: ergon tool run [options] TOOL [ARGUMENTS...]

Install a tool of a section and run it.

ergon tool run installs the tool that a section of .ergon.yaml names, unless
the cache has it, and runs it in the working directory with the arguments that
follow the tool. It installs the tool under ergon/tools in the cache directory
of the user, and checks a release binary against the digest that the section
states for the platform. It reads the options of the repository of the working
directory or of the nearest of its parents with .ergon/init.lock.

The exit status is the exit status of the tool. It is 1 when the tool does not
install, and 2 when the section or the tool does not exist.

Example:
  ergon tool run go.golangci-lint -- run ./...

Arguments:
      TOOL       Tool to run, as <section>.<tool>.
      ARGUMENTS  Arguments of the tool. Pass them after --.  default ""

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon tool path --help
Usage: ergon tool path [options] TOOL

Install a tool of a section and print its program.

ergon tool path installs the tool that a section of .ergon.yaml names, unless
the cache has it, as ergon tool run does, and prints the path of its program. A
Makefile or a script then passes the path to a program that starts the tool,
such as zig as the C compiler of a build. A tool that runs through another
program, such as an npm package that npx runs, has no program of its own.

The exit status is 1 when the tool does not install or has no program of its
own, and 2 when the section or the tool does not exist.

Example:
  ergon tool path go.zig

Arguments:
      TOOL  Tool to print the program of, as <section>.<tool>.

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon tool prune --help
Usage: ergon tool prune [options]

Remove the tools that no section of .ergon.yaml names.

ergon tool prune removes each file from ergon/tools in the cache directory of
the user that installs no tool of the sections of .ergon.yaml at the version
that they name: the earlier versions of the tools, the programs of a Go module
for another version of the go command, the programs of golangci-lint for other
plugins, and the files of an install that did not finish. It also removes the
tools of other repositories that share the directory. Each job of the managed
workflows that keeps the tools of ergon in the cache of GitHub Actions runs it
before the cache saves the directory.

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon tool ci prune --help
Usage: ergon tool ci prune [options]

Delete the tool caches that newer caches replaced.

ergon tool ci prune deletes each cache of the tools of ergon in GitHub Actions
that a newer cache of the same job replaced, through the API of GitHub with the
token of GITHUB_TOKEN, which needs the permission actions: write. A job saves a
cache under a new key for each change of the files of its key, and restores
only the newest cache of its own when its key misses. The caches of a branch and
of a pull request are separate.

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon tool run
ergon: tool run: missing argument TOOL
[exit 2]

$ ergon tool run biome
ergon: cli: "biome", which is not <section>.<tool>
[exit 2]

$ ergon tool run js.prettier
ergon: tool: the section names no such tool: js.prettier, which is none of js.biome
[exit 2]

$ ergon tool run go.vet
ergon: baseline: no producer of the repository has the section: "go"
[exit 2]

$ ergon tool path js.biome
ergon: tool: the tool does not install: js.biome runs through npx
[exit 1]

$ ergon tool path js.prettier
ergon: tool: the section names no such tool: js.prettier, which is none of js.biome
[exit 2]

$ ergon tool prune main
ergon: tool prune: unexpected argument "main"
[exit 2]

$ ergon tool ci prune main
ergon: tool ci prune: unexpected argument "main"
[exit 2]
